newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch PTT 1996 net seen rising 8-10 pct.
newsitem.headline: Dutch PTT 1996 net seen rising 8-10 pct.

text.p: Dutch post and telecoms group PTT Nederland NV (KPN) is on course for an eight to 10 percent rise in net profit when it reports 1996 figures on Tuesday, boosted by rising volumes and cost-cuts, analysts say.

Forecasts for 1996 net profit range from 2.440 billion to 2.482 billion guilders, up from the previous 2.257 billion. The company said in January that sales had reached 21 billion guilders in 1996, compared to 19.15 billion in 1995.
It also said net profit rose "significantly" in 1996. A KPN spokeswoman on Friday said, by Dutch corporate yardsticks, such a move points to a 7-12 percent increase.
"The company has already indicated the sort of increase they're looking for," said Joost van Beek of Van Meer James Capel, adding he was looking for net profit of 2.46 billion.
Analysts said they were expecting a rise in the company's dividend payout to around to 2.80-2.90 guilders, up from the 2.60 per share for 1995.

"Both sides of the company will see growth but I think the majority will be related to post," he said, noting the company should benefit from continuing cost cutting and efficiency improvements at the units as well as an increase in tariffs.
International telephony, investing heavily abroad, was feeling the pinch from pressurised margins.
"There's still good growth in the domestic telephony market," added Van Beek.
James Downie of ABN AMRO Hoare Govett said he was looking for 2.447 billion guilders net with a dividend of 2.80 guilders.
"In the postal side we are looking for pretty reasonable volume growth coming through," he said. "We're seeing decent sales growth with (group) sales of over 21 billion guilders."

Downie said he would be listening for news of the new value added telephony services the company was launching such as call waiting and forwarding, which should have an impact on volumes for the telephony unit.

"We are looking for higher call volumes. They have been cutting some of their international call charges so we would expect the elasticity factor to boost volumes there, and with higher advertising we'll be looking for something on the local side as well," said Downie.

"I think we'll be hearing some more details on the reorganisation of the telephones business with the integration of some of the regional offices in to the central organisation and hopefully get some more details on the TNT deal," he said.
KPN in October agreed the 2.7 billion guilder buy of Australia's TNT transport company.

"If the company can get a little more upbeat (at the results news conference) it could be good news for the shares. They're still looking a bit undervalued. I don't think the full benefits of the TNT deal have been factored into the share price," he said. The shares were at 67.00 guilders on Friday afternoon. -- Keiron Henderson, Amsterdam Newsroom +31 20 504 5000
